title: Lab session: streaming + tool validation sprint notes
content:
Context and motivation:
We ran a two-week prototyping sprint for an end-to-end developer flow that: streams partial text, invokes deterministic tool calls mid-stream, and returns a typed final payload (JSON envelope + artifacts). This doc captures the lab experiments, quick wins, UX prompts for SDK ergonomics, and validation checklist we can iterate on before a wider PRD.

High-level goals (non-exhaustive):
- Make incremental streaming predictable for client-side SDKs: hooks that surface stable partial output, signal tool intent, and allow client prefetching.
- Define a minimal, backwards-compatible structured-output envelope that supports tool results, diagnostics, and progressive checkpoints.
- Surface ergonomic SDK patterns for auth, backpressure, and resume for flaky mobile networks.
- Create automated tests and golden prompts that detect regressions in structured fidelity and tool call determinism.

What we built in the lab (short):
1) Handshake shim: small JSON-first header that advertises session capabilities (prefetch, typed-output, resume-token). Implemented in the dev runtime (nginx + node proxy) as header X-RW-Session-Cap.
2) Streaming frame format: compact newline-delimited frames: "meta", "delta", "toolcall", "commit". Frames are idempotent and include sequence indices and optional resume tokens.
3) Tool-call envelope: a toolcall frame that contains tool_id, args (opaque JSON), expected_response_schema (optional), and handoff_hint (sync|async).
4) Structured commit: final "commit" frame delivers final envelope: {status, outputs, artifacts[], traces[]}. We prototyped a stable schema and validator.

Key design decisions and tradeoffs observed:
- Inline vs out-of-band tool responses:
  * Inline (tool result in the stream) keeps a single canonical timeline but makes the stream heavier; easier for clients that rehydrate session state.
  * Out-of-band (tool results uploaded to artifact store with ref in stream) reduces bandwidth but requires durable storage + lookup; better for binary artifacts.
  Outcome: default to inline for small tool results (<= 4KB JSON) and out-of-band for larger blobs with a signed URL reference.

- Sequence numbering and resume semantics:
  * Use monotonically increasing frame_seq + periodic resume_token in meta frames. Client can resume by asking for next_seq > last_seen.
  * Tradeoff: extra tokens increase payload but vastly reduces duplicate processing complexity. Recommendation: include resume token every 8 frames by default.

SDK ergonomics experiments (notes):
- JS SDK (node/browser) prototype surfaces three main hooks: onPartial(delta), onToolCall(toolMeta), onComplete(envelope). We experimented with a small Promise/async-iterator wrapper that returns:
  const s = client.streamCall(req);
  for await (const frame of s) { /* frames typed: delta|tool|meta|commit */ }
  This felt ergonomic in Node and React suspensy scenarios.
- Mobile-friendly wrapper: an event-emitter with checkpoint persistence to localStorage/Sqlite. Exposed methods: pause(), resume(), lastCheckpoint().
- Backpressure: implemented a token-based window (client advertises window_n frames it can accept). Server honors window and queues; default window 16 frames.

Test harness and golden prompts:
- Created a small test harness that runs variations: concurrent tool calls, tool errors, mid-stream model hallucination, and resume after network flake. Tests assert: final schema validity, tool-call ordering, and no silent drops.
- Golden prompts: three short prompts that exercise tool chain:
  1) "Summarize and lookup price of product X; if price > $100 attach price-check artifact via price_checker tool."
  2) "Walk me through a two-step API workflow, call verifier tool to validate JSON."
  3) "Multi-turn fragment: ask clarifying Qs, then synthesize and call code-runner tool to return snippet."
- We store golden-run outputs in CI and run diff + structural lint on the structured envelope.

Schema sketch (lab version) — kept intentionally compact in doc:
- commit.envelope: {
    "status": "ok|partial|failed",
    "outputs": [ { "name": string, "type": string, "value": any } ],
    "tools": [ { "tool_id": string, "phase": "prefetch|invoke|post", "result_ref": string|object } ],
    "artifacts": [ { "id": string, "mime": string, "ref": string } ],
    "telemetry": { "latency_ms": number, "token_count": number }
  }
Note: values above are lab placeholders; validator implemented in typescript and used for CI in the lab repo.

Operational and failure modes we observed:
- Tool timeouts while mid-stream: client should surface a "tool_pending" partial state and optionally render earlier deltas. Server-side we defaulted to soft-timeout 6s then fallback.
- Double-emit when resume overlaps: sequence + resume token approach eliminated state conflicts in >95% runs. Remaining cases were caused by heuristic-based edge replays (we added a server-side dedupe cache keyed by session_id+frame_seq).
- Cost: inline tool responses increase token accounting ambiguity. We added a flag for billing separation: tool result tokens can be billed as separate line items in request meta. Need PM/finance review.

Open questions (needs decisions):
- Strongly typed tool contracts vs weak/opt-in schemas: what do we require for GA? Full typing increases onboarding friction but lowers runtime surprises. Proposal: opt-in strong typing for enterprise accounts; weak schemas for public.
- Resume token cadence: 8 frames vs 16 frames? Next sprint, run perf tests with 10k concurrent sessions to evaluate memory/latency tradeoff.
- SDK surface for partial structured assertions: should we provide a small validator dependency or expect clients to reuse server-provided PDP (portable validator payload)?
- Billing model on tool-call tokens: single invoice vs split. Sync with finance.

Acceptance criteria for next milestone (end of Q):
- SDKs (JS + Py) expose streaming iterator and toolcall hooks with stable public examples in the dev docs.
- Lab validator (typescript) included in repo, runs in CI and blocks PRs that change root schema.
- Golden prompt suite (10 prompts) integrated into nightly CI with alerts on structural diffs.
- Decide typing policy for tool contracts and document API for opt-in strong typing.

Action items / owners:
- Add final schema PR and typescript validator: Ethan Zhao (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-sdk/pull/342) — due 2025-10-08.
- Billing proposal for tool tokens: Carlos Mendes — draft to finance by 2025-10-15.
- JS SDK iterator API polish and examples: Maya Patel + Lena Ortiz — update docs + cookbooks by 2025-11-01.
- Scale perf run (10k sessions) for resume token cadence: infra SRE (tag: eng-sre) — run in staging 2025-11-05.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally experimental: we favored pragmatic, developer-observable patterns over theoretical purity. Expect rough edges; call out risk areas and strong objections.
- If you want to run the lab locally: repo instructions in linked_artifacts PR + run "yarn dev:stream-lab". There is a small docker-compose that spins up the mock tool service.

Appendix (short):
- Quick snippets: sample toolcall frame: { "frame_type": "toolcall", "frame_seq": 37, "payload": { "tool_id": "price_checker:v1", "args": {"sku": "X-123"}, "expect_schema": {"price": "number"} } }
- Resume header example: `X-RW-Resume: session=js-sess-7;last_seq=40;token=eyJ...`

End.
